notes: Cross-platform unit/integration tests on Ubuntu 24.04 AMD64/ARM64 Node 22/24 remain green. A separate real-systemd CI matrix has six passing jobs: two transient services, two dedicated native nologin account installations, and two native PostgreSQL17 owner-onboarding integrations on AMD64 and ARM64. Each PostgreSQL-onboarding job creates an isolated disposable CI DB, executes the migration and one-time console owner bootstrap tools distributed in a VERIFIED signed source bundle, validates a separately credentialed application PostgreSQL runtime role can read/write ordinary data but CANNOT CREATE tables, then runs the root-owned signed Domyro service as a dedicated unprivileged systemd account. HTTP authentication, site/room creation and persistence across normal restart and SIGKILL recovery were demonstrated while unsafe update installation remained blocked (D-53). No one-command public Ubuntu installer, production secure onboarding or HTTPS, managed/external service choices, full DB/config/Matter recovery, true update worker, bare-metal/VM reboot acceptance or owner deployment approval. Every D-53 readiness check is FALSE and ownerDeploymentConsentRecorded is FALSE. Draft integration PR #4 additionally proves: offline, independently pinned Ed25519 source package admission from actual files; rejects modified artifact, signature, extra entry, and tampered high-water release receipt before staging; starts a real restricted-user native systemd/PostgreSQL integration on disposable Ubuntu amd64/arm64; protects already existing installations including after SIGKILL; and tests a fsynced, strictly ordered isolated firstboot intent journal. All 8 integrated CI jobs have passed at commit 1de9d00b. These are development checks and do not establish owner/server deployment readiness. D-53 installation checks and owner consent remain FALSE. CI extension (2026-11-02): firstboot journal phases are now recorded against actual signed-file provenance, installed dependencies, PostgreSQL owner and non-DDL runtime role, service user/systemd liveness, and persistent HTTP onboarding. Four failpoints verify durable phase before abort; a parent process independently reads the retained firstboot journal after real installer SIGKILL, before explicit disposable cleanup. PostgreSQL database creation happens only after signed source and locked dependencies pass. This is CI-only evidence, not a production transaction, and does not unlock D-53. CI extension 2026-11-02: a native firstboot PostgreSQL database snapshot is encrypted with DOMYROS2 and independently restored into a brand-new scratch database; real user/site/membership/room hashes must match and source DB remain untouched. Wrong passwords, altered ciphertext and nonempty target restore attempts are rejected. A private selected-config snapshot of the CI instance's actual systemd unit and runtime environment is similarly encrypted and restored to scratch. After true installer SIGKILL, the independent parent restores both backups again, preserving running services and rejecting a second installer. Only CI-only ephemeral files, PostgreSQL databases, and GitHub-hosted VMs are touched; no persistent production key, Matter fabric backup, atomic whole-system snapshot or recovery wizard exists. 2026-11-02 device prototype: a hardened Zigbee2MQTT exposes parser grants narrow light/switch ON/OFF and bounded brightness capabilities only when published metadata explicitly allows read+write. An isolated command controller sends only explicit operator-confirmed commands to a test-provided MQTT publisher; physical success is never inferred from QoS1 PUBACK, only from a newer observed non-retained state for the same IEEE identity. Real ephemeral Aedes MQTT broker tests confirm success/timeout and no observer publishing; negative tests cover retained/stale states, unsupported devices, multi-endpoint, rename, cooldown, crash/offline and prohibited commands. An authenticated site-scoped read-only GET devices API and a real-data-only Dutch/English dashboard are added. This does NOT wire commands to any live device or authorize hardware or production deployment. 2026-11-02 one-line and updates priority: versioned GitHub release downloader now requires a separately pinned Ed25519 publisher SPKI fingerprint and verifies the complete AMD64+ARM64 source artifacts before returning a private downloaded package, rejecting redirects, tampering and oversized content. A separate GitHub latest release discovery module only proposes untrusted SemVer, which cannot install or update without authenticated release bytes. The guarded release CLI ships inside signed source archives and supports check/prepare while install/update stay blocked (exit 53). A workflow for draft official release publication is checked into the integration branch, requiring all D-53 checks, an approved production-release environment, and an owner-managed signing secret; publisher config remains unconfigured and no official release has been published. Neither a bootstrap that installs a fresh Ubuntu host in one command nor a production service update worker exists yet.
